articles.title: The Verifier's Dilemma: Why Honest AI Needs a Bounty, Not Just a Bond
articles.description: Bond-and-slash verifiable AI assumes someone audits. But checking costs money and pays nothing, so a rational verifier won't — the verifier's dilemma. Proof of Sampling fixes it with a bounty, and the math says honest inference holds at a 0.74% sampling rate where nobody ever arbitrates.

articles.title: Clipped to Consensus: How Yuma Scores Subjective AI
articles.description: Decentralized AI networks have to turn many validators' subjective quality scores into one reward number. Bittensor's Yuma Consensus uses a stake-weighted median and clips the rest — robust to a <50% bloc. Then a parasite shows up: copying the consensus pays better than producing it.

articles.title: Acting on a Stale Policy: The Asynchrony Budget in Decentralized RL
articles.description: Decentralized RL splits the actor from the learner across the internet: the policy a worker acts with runs several steps behind the one that learns. INTELLECT-2 held reward at 4 steps stale; SparrowRL cut the broadcast 79x. The bandwidth and staleness taxes, and what the chain secures.

articles.title: The Batch You Can't Fill: The Hidden Tax on Decentralized LLM Inference
articles.description: Verification overhead gets the blame, but the real tax on decentralized LLM inference is the batch a single-tenant node can't fill. On identical 8x H100s, Llama-3.3-70B costs about $258 per million tokens at batch 1 and $2.30 at batch 256 — a 112x spread. Why, and how networks fight it.

articles.title: Minutes Per Token: The Cost of Blind LLM Inference
articles.description: Secure multi-party computation runs a transformer without any party seeing your prompt — at minutes per query and gigabytes per token. BumbleBee's BERT-base: 6.4 GB, 2.55 min; LLaMA-7B: ~8 min/token. The bytes don't go where you'd think, and it's why 'blind' networks fall back to TEEs.

articles.title: Prove the Neighbors, Not the Sort: Verifiable Retrieval for Untrusted RAG
articles.description: An AI agent that retrieves from an untrusted vector DB can't tell the true top-k from a cherry-picked or fabricated one. Re-running the search needs the whole corpus. The 2026 fix: commit the snapshot, then prove the k-th distance is a boundary, not the sort. V3DB proves it 22x faster.

articles.title: A Hash Is Not a Model: The Storage Bill Behind On-Chain AI
articles.description: On-chain AI loves to say a model is 'stored on-chain.' But a chain commits to a 32-byte hash for cents; keeping the 140 GB it points to retrievable is a separate, recurring, surprisingly centralized bill. The storage math, erasure coding, and the retrieval wall.

articles.title: Proving a Model Forgot: Verifiable Unlearning and the Immutable Ledger
articles.description: A DataDAO sold your data; you invoke the right to be forgotten. Deleting the file is easy, but the model already learned and the ledger can't be rewritten. ZK-APEX proves the unlearning ran in ~2h; UMA still pulls the 'forgotten' data back at MIA 0.97. Certified isn't forgotten.

articles.title: Cheaper to Break Than to Defend: The Economics of Autonomous Exploit Agents
articles.description: An LLM agent that writes its own working smart-contract exploit isn't hypothetical: A1 hits 63% on real exploited contracts and once pulled $8.59M from a single bug. The economics are the story — at a few dollars a scan, attackers profit at a tenth the contract value defenders need.

articles.title: The 78% Oracle: How AI Resolves Prediction Markets — and Who Catches the Mistakes
articles.description: AI agents now resolve most prediction markets straight off the web — UMA's bot hits 99.3% on sports and 72% on mention markets. The optimistic oracle's dispute game is the backstop, but it only catches errors someone is paid to catch. The numbers, and the silent-settlement gap.

articles.title: The Liquidation Goes to Auction: Recapturing Oracle-Extractable Value
articles.description: A DeFi liquidation mints a fixed prize, and for years it went to whoever won the gas war, not the protocol. Aave's own data shows Chainlink SVR routing $675M of liquidations and clawing ~$16M back. Inside the recapture-auction mechanics — SVR, Oval, API3 — and what they don't fix.

articles.title: Phantom GPUs: Verifying Real Hardware in Trustless Compute Networks
articles.description: A decentralized GPU network has to answer two questions an AWS invoice never raises: is this the GPU it claims, and did it actually do the work? io.net logged 327,000 registered GPUs and roughly 6,720 daily-verified. We dissect metadata trust, PoW puzzles, performance fingerprinting, and zkGPU-ID.

articles.title: Grading Their Own Homework: The Evaluator Gap in On-Chain Agent Commerce
articles.description: Virtuals' Agent Commerce Protocol sells an independent evaluator as the thing that makes agents trust each other's work. We read 62,882 jobs off Base — and in a 30-job sample, every one let the buyer grade itself. Not one used a third party.

articles.title: Agents Hiring Agents: The On-Chain SLA Inside Olas's Mech Marketplace
articles.description: Olas turned an off-chain AI task into an on-chain contract: 2.1M requests across 100 mechs, a 60-300s priority window, and a Karma ledger that docks no-shows. We read the marketplace off Gnosis and dissect its crypto-economic SLA.

articles.title: Fingerprints in the Weights: Monetizing Open AI Models You Can't Lock
articles.description: You can copy open model weights bit-for-bit, so on-chain ownership can't be cryptographically enforced — only proven. Sentient's answer: fine-tune 24,576 secret key-response fingerprints into the weights and make scale the security parameter.

articles.title: Picking Off the Pool: The Arbitrage Tax on AMM Liquidity Providers
articles.description: Passive AMM liquidity is a short option that arbitrage bots exercise every block. LVR = σ²/8 prices the rent — at ETH's 63% realized vol that's ~5% of pool value a year, and most pools don't earn enough fees to cover it. The math, real numbers, and the auctions clawing it back.

articles.title: Don't Average, Anticipate: Allora's Context-Aware Inference Synthesis
articles.description: Most decentralized-AI networks vote or average. Allora bets the network should learn whom to trust per context — using forecasters that predict who's about to be wrong, mapped to weights through a softplus gradient. We dissect the mechanism, the math, and where it pays.

articles.title: The Sandwich Tax on Autonomous Agents
articles.description: An autonomous agent that swaps in the open broadcasts its intent to every searcher in the mempool. We solve the optimal sandwich on a live Base pool, show why an agent's slippage default is the searcher's profit knob, and price the defenses.

articles.title: Bait and Switch: Auditing Model Substitution in Decentralized Inference Markets
articles.description: You pay per token for a named model; the provider picks the precision. FP8 quantization costs 0.6 MMLU points and is near-invisible to output auditing — so inference markets bond and attest instead of detect.

articles.title: Provenance Isn't Purity: Data Poisoning and the Limits of On-Chain Data Markets
articles.description: A landmark 2025 result: ~250 poisoned documents backdoor an LLM whether it has 600M or 13B parameters — 0.00016% of the tokens. DataDAOs sell 'verifiable' training data, but on-chain provenance proves integrity, not purity. Here's the gap, and what actually narrows it.

articles.title: Graduate or Die: The Bonding Curve Behind Tokenized AI Agents
articles.description: Launching an AI agent token is one constant-product auction. We read Virtuals' Bonding contract off Base: a 6,000-VIRTUAL virtual reserve, a 64× price ramp, graduation at exactly 42,000 VIRTUAL, and the 12.5% gap where the Uniswap pool opens below the curve.

articles.title: Rate-Chasers: Why DeFi Yield Agents Win Where Trading Bots Lose
articles.description: Autonomous agents run ~19% of on-chain activity and beat Aave and Morpho at stablecoin yield — yet lose to humans at trading by 5 to 1. The split isn't about model quality. Yield-chasing is a constrained optimization against a kinked rate curve; trading needs alpha agents don't have.

articles.title: The 3% Spoof: Can You Prove a Decentralized Model Was Actually Trained?
articles.description: Permissionless training networks pay peers for gradients they can't re-run. Proof-of-Learning was meant to verify the work — until it was forged for 3% of the training cost, then for one floating-point op per weight. Here's the mechanism, the attacks, and what's deployed instead.

articles.title: The Cognitive Penalty: When AI DAO Delegates Reason Their Way to Yes
articles.description: Wire an LLM into a Governor contract and the proposal text becomes the attack surface. A frozen-weights ablation finds the twist: turning on deliberation drops adversarial robustness from 100% to 68.5% — and the 226s it takes to think is itself extractable value.

articles.title: What's Your Data Worth? Valuing Contributions in On-Chain Data Markets
articles.description: DataDAOs promise to pay you for your data — but 'pay you fairly' hides a cooperative-game problem that's O(2ⁿ). Inside Data Shapley, the KNN trick that makes it tractable, why rankings flip under SGD noise, and what Vana's Proof of Contribution actually computes instead.

articles.title: It Isn't the Model: The Operating Layer Behind 7.5M On-Chain Agent Trades
articles.description: DX Terminal Pro ran 3,505 LLM agents trading real ETH on Base for 21 days: 7.5M invocations, ~$20M volume, 99.9% settlement. The reliability came from the operating layer around the model, not the weights — here are the numbers and the failure modes.

articles.title: Same Prompt, Different Bytes: The Determinism Problem Under Verifiable On-Chain AI
articles.description: Every on-chain scheme that verifies an LLM by re-executing it and comparing digests assumes a forward pass is bit-for-bit reproducible. It isn't — Thinking Machines got 80 different answers to one prompt at temperature 0. Here's why, and what determinism costs.

articles.title: Fake Memories, Real Transfers: Context-Injection Attacks on On-Chain AI Agents
articles.description: An agent doesn't need its key stolen to drain a wallet — it can be talked into signing. CrAIBench shows memory injection beating prompt injection 55% to ~0% on the strongest model, and only fine-tuning closes the gap.

articles.title: Don't Vote, Rank: Peer-Ranked Consensus for Decentralized LLM Swarms
articles.description: Majority voting over LLMs throws away the one node that got it right. Fortytwo's swarm inference ranks answers pairwise instead — +17 points on GPQA Diamond — with on-chain reputation and proof-of-capability for Sybil defense. The mechanism, the math, the tradeoffs.

articles.title: The Gas Wall: What It Costs to Run a Neural Net Inside the EVM
articles.description: Most 'on-chain AI' keeps the model off-chain and posts a proof. But you can also just run the forward pass in Solidity. We do the gas math — ~106k gas per weight, an MNIST net that needs 180 Ethereum blocks — and find the thin band of models that fit.

articles.title: What the Agent Saw: zkTLS and the Web-Proof Trust Stack
articles.description: An AI agent that acts on your bank balance has to prove it saw that balance — without a trusted API. zkTLS turns any HTTPS session into a portable proof. We dissect MPC-TLS vs proxy vs TEE, the real TLSNotary benchmarks, and read Reclaim's on-chain verifier on Base down to its single attestor.

articles.title: Bond It, Don't Prove It: Restaking and the Cost of Corrupting an AI Oracle
articles.description: zkML, optimistic, TEE, FHE all prove the computation. Restaking takes the other road: bond it and slash liars. We do the cost-of-corruption math behind EigenLayer's $18B AI-AVS security, the overloading attack that breaks it, and the probabilistic-audit tax.

articles.title: Betting Machines: How LLM Agents Trade On-Chain Prediction Markets
articles.description: Yesterday an AI agent deployed a prediction market on Gnosis; other agents will price it, bet on it, and resolve it. The calibration data behind LLM forecasters, the FPMM math they trade against, and what breaks when the marginal bettor is a model.

articles.title: Who Gets Paid When AI Remixes IP? Reading Story's Royalty Graph Off the Chain
articles.description: Story raised $140M to make IP programmable for the AI era. We read its chain: 6.46M registered IP assets, 230,300 licenses ever minted, one week of royalties totaling $10 — plus the LAP/LRP royalty math and the precompile at 0x0101 that computes the graph.

articles.title: Agent Keys and the Blast Radius Problem: Custody Engineering with EIP-7702 and Spend Permissions
articles.description: An agent holding your raw key is one prompt injection from total loss — and 97% of early EIP-7702 delegations went to drainer sweepers. We read the sweeper's source off the chain, dissect a real 35.97-USDC-a-day spend permission on Base, and do the blast-radius math.

articles.title: Proof of Personhood vs. the Agent Flood: Inside World ID and Priority Blockspace for Humans
articles.description: World Chain reserved top-of-block space for verified humans while 382M smart-account ops poured in. We read the Semaphore tree on Ethereum — 17.59M identities, hourly batches at ~3,300 gas each — decode PBH's month-stamped nullifiers, and find the human-only lane sitting almost empty.

articles.title: When the Graph Misleads: GNNs vs. Gradient-Boosted Trees in On-Chain Fraud Detection
articles.description: The Elliptic benchmark made GNNs the default for on-chain AML. A 2026 leakage-free re-evaluation flips the script: random forests win by 13 F1 points, randomly rewired edges beat the real graph, and every model falls off a cliff at time step 43.

articles.title: Burn, Mint, or Bid: How Decentralized GPU Markets Price Compute
articles.description: Render just voted to route 60,000 Salad GPUs' payments through a token burn; Akash auctions its 234 GPUs per-block on-chain. Two opposed pricing mechanisms, live H100 quotes, and the burn-vs-emission math the equilibrium story skips.

articles.title: FHE Hits Mainnet: What Private On-Chain Compute Actually Costs
articles.description: FHE left the lab: confidential ERC-7984 tokens settle on Ethereum for ~$0.09 in gas, with 48,000 transfers since December. We dissect a live encrypted transaction, the 13-node MPC committee underneath, and why encrypted inference is still 11 seconds per token.

articles.title: From Price to Flow: How Bittensor Re-Plumbed Its Emission Engine
articles.description: Bittensor let AMM prices decide which AI subnets earn 3,600 TAO a day — until a memecoin subnet gamed the formula. Inside the TaoFlow upgrade: the constant-product math that got exploited, the EMA flow accounting that replaced it, and why refundable manipulation is the design smell to hunt for.

articles.title: What the Blockchain Actually Does in Decentralized AI Training
articles.description: The gradients never touch the chain. What Solana actually stores when Psyche trains a 36B model across 24 nodes, how TOPLOC audits untrusted GPUs in 258 bytes, and why the flagship 'decentralized' model still shipped from a 512-GPU cluster.

articles.title: ERC-8004 in the Wild: Auditing the Trustless Agents Registries On-Chain
articles.description: ERC-8004's agent registries went live in January. We read them straight off the chain: ~90,000 registrations across Ethereum and Base, a $0.003 ERC-4337 registration dissected — and a reputation registry already farmed with vouch spam.

articles.title: Dissecting a 1.3-Cent Agent Payment: x402 on Base, by the Numbers
articles.description: We pulled a live x402 settlement off Base: a $0.013 USDC transfer relayed by a facilitator wallet with a nonce past 1.7 million, at an 11% gas-to-value ratio. What on-chain evidence and 100M transactions actually say about the agent economy.

articles.title: The Solver Optimization Market: How Intent-Based DEXes Auction Your Trade
articles.description: Intent-based DEXes don't route your trade — they auction it. Solvers compete as autonomous optimizers to settle a batch at one clearing price. Inside CoW Protocol's contract, the optimization problem, and the metaheuristic solvers now winning it.

articles.title: TEE-Attested Inference: Verifiable AI at Hardware Speed
articles.description: zkML costs 1000x, optimistic schemes cost a challenge window. Hardware attestation verifies AI inference at under 7% overhead and ~$0.26 on-chain — if you're willing to trust Intel. Part 3 weighs the third leg of verifiable inference.

articles.title: Agents That Pay: How x402 Settles a Stablecoin Payment On-Chain
articles.description: An agent hits an API, gets HTTP 402, signs a stablecoin authorization, and a facilitator settles it on-chain for a fraction of a cent. We trace one real payment on Base down to the gas — and where the trust actually sits.

articles.title: How AI Agents Pay for APIs: Inside x402 and Gasless Stablecoin Settlement
articles.description: An autonomous agent can't sign up for an API key or swipe a credit card. x402 revives HTTP 402 and settles in gasless USDC — here's the EIP-3009 handshake, the facilitator trust model, and where prompt injection breaks it.

articles.title: Optimistic ML Oracles: Verifiable Inference Without the Proof Overhead
articles.description: Zero-knowledge proofs aren't the only path to trustworthy on-chain AI. Optimistic schemes trade latency for a 1000x cost reduction — here's how dispute games over inference actually work.

articles.title: Agentic Smart-Contract Auditing: What LLM Swarms Catch (and Miss)
articles.description: We ran multi-agent LLM pipelines against historical exploit corpora and live audit engagements. The results reshape where AI fits in a security review — and where it absolutely doesn't.

articles.title: zkML in 2026: The State of Verifiable Inference
articles.description: Zero-knowledge proofs promised to make machine learning trustless. A field survey of where zkML actually stands — proving systems, quantization tradeoffs, and what's deployable today.

artifacts.title: The Sampling Threshold
artifacts.description: An inspection game between a solver and a verifier. Drag the operating rate and tune the bond, reward, and bounty to find p*, the minimum sampling rate that makes honest AI inference a dominant strategy — and watch it collapse without a bounty.

artifacts.title: The Consensus Clip
artifacts.description: Bittensor's Yuma Consensus scores a miner by the stake-weighted median of validator weights, then clips everything above it. Validators sit on a cumulative-stake axis; the consensus line is read at the κ=50% mark. Push a colluding bloc past 50% and watch the pump go from clipped to unstoppable.

artifacts.title: The Staleness Clock
artifacts.description: In decentralized RL the rollout worker acts with a policy several steps behind the trainer. Staleness g = broadcast time / step cadence. Pick a model and link, toggle sparse deltas, and watch g cross INTELLECT-2's demonstrated 4-step budget — full 32B weights blow right past it.

artifacts.title: The Decentralization Tax
artifacts.description: Cost per million tokens and throughput for Llama 3.3 70B on 8x H100 as the batch fills. A single-tenant node (B=1) runs ~25 tok/s at ~$258/M; a filled batch (B=256) runs ~2,800 tok/s at ~$2.30/M — same silicon, 112x cheaper. Pick a batch; read the tax you pay for the GPU you can't fill.

artifacts.title: The Nonlinearity Tax
artifacts.description: Under secure two-party inference, a transformer's cost is eaten by Softmax and GELU, not the matrix multiplies. Stacked per-operation communication and interaction rounds for one BERT-base block across Iron, BumbleBee, and Nimbus — the nonlinear activations are 80–95% of the bill.

artifacts.title: The Sort Tax
artifacts.description: Proving an agent's top-k retrieval is real costs a sort over every scanned candidate, unless you prove a boundary instead. Drive top-k and the corpus preset; watch the in-circuit comparison count split into the flat boundary proof and the sort tax you skip, anchored to V3DB's measured 22x.

artifacts.title: The Weight Vault
artifacts.description: A chain commits to a model's 32-byte hash for cents; keeping the gigabytes it points to retrievable is a separate, recurring bill. Pick a model and horizon and watch three rent-charging storage layers race Arweave's pay-once permanence to a crossover — plus the on-chain byte cost and cold-load wall.

artifacts.title: The Unlearning Gap
artifacts.description: What unlearning verification reports as 'forgotten' versus what a recovery attack gets back. Each method's dumbbell runs from its verdict (MIA ≈ random) to what an attack recovers — 0.97–0.99 for cheap methods. Toggle to % recoverable; tap a method. The ZK proof's scope ends at the verdict.

artifacts.title: The Exploit Asymmetry
artifacts.description: When an LLM agent writes the exploit, the fight is unit economics. Break-even contract value against cost-per-scan: the attacker's line, and the defender's sitting 10× higher because a bounty pays a tenth of a theft. The band between is the attacker-only zone, with A1's six models at measured cost.

artifacts.title: The Watcher's Threshold
artifacts.description: An AI proposer is wrong a few percent of the time, but UMA pays a winning disputer only half the bond it risks — so the break-even belief is two-thirds, not half. Every category's base error rate sits deep in the no-dispute zone; raise the reward and the threshold slides left.

artifacts.title: The Liquidation Value Split
artifacts.description: A liquidation mints a fixed prize — the bonus on seized collateral. Three bars split it three ways: a gas war bleeds it to the block builder, private orderflow pockets it for the searcher, an OEV auction returns ~73% to the protocol. Drive size, bonus, competition; anchored to Chainlink SVR figures.

artifacts.title: The Hardware Fingerprint
artifacts.description: Pick the GPU a provider bills for and the cheaper card it secretly runs; the network measures the real device's compute, bandwidth and VRAM and plots it against the claimed model's fingerprint. Watch the spoof land outside the tolerance band — or hide inside it.

artifacts.title: The Evaluator's Chair
artifacts.description: Drive a Virtuals ACP escrow job: client funds USDC, provider submits a deliverable hash, and whoever sits in the evaluator's chair springs the payout. Seat the client (what ~all of Base does), a neutral agent, or no one — then run it or let someone cheat, and watch who's left exposed.

artifacts.title: The Forfeit Window
artifacts.description: A single mech request, drivable: drag the priority mech's response time across the 60-300s window. Inside it the priority mech delivers and gains Karma; past it a backup delivers, the priority mech forfeits the fee and is docked Karma. Live Olas marketplace constants.

artifacts.title: The Fingerprint Reserve
artifacts.description: Open weights can't be locked, so ownership is proven by counting surviving fingerprints. Embed thousands of secret key-response pairs; an adversary fine-tunes to scrub them and each audit burns one to leakage. Watch the reserve survive — or not.

artifacts.title: The LP Break-Even Frontier
artifacts.description: Does an AMM LP out-earn the arbitrage bots picking off its stale quotes? Plot fee income (flat) against LVR = σ²/8 (rising with vol²): where they cross is break-even. At low turnover even BTC sits in the red. Flip on solver-auction recapture and the frontier slides right.

artifacts.title: The Regret Lens
artifacts.description: Allora weights models by regret, not votes. Drag a market from calm to a volatility spike: five forecasters ride the softplus weight curve φ′(R̂), the low-vol specialist collapses the instant a spike is forecast while the vol-aware model climbs. Tap a model for its R→R̂→w chain.

artifacts.title: Sandwich Simulator
artifacts.description: Watch a searcher sandwich your agent's swap on the live Aerodrome WETH/USDC pool on Base. Set trade size and slippage tolerance; the optimal front-run is solved on the real constant-product curve, capped by your tolerance. Route privately and the extraction goes to zero.

artifacts.title: The Detection Cliff
artifacts.description: How many audit probes it takes to catch a substituted model, as a function of how subtle the swap is. A 1/Δ² curve over real quantization accuracy gaps: a model swap is caught in a few hundred probes; FP8 needs ~150k and falls off the cliff into the economically-invisible zone.

artifacts.title: The Dilution Myth
artifacts.description: The same 250-document backdoor that compromised LLMs from 600M to 13B params, plotted across model scale. Toggle 'documents needed' — a flat 250 vs the myth that poison scales with data — and 'share of training set', collapsing to 0.00016% and below. Drag to pick a scale.

artifacts.title: The Graduation Curve
artifacts.description: Walk the real bonding curve that prices a tokenized AI agent: 6,000 virtual VIRTUAL against 1B tokens on a constant product, spot ramping 64× to graduation at 42,000 VIRTUAL. The shaded area is VIRTUAL raised; toggle the halfway split to see the first 21,000 buy ~89% of supply.

artifacts.title: The Attestation Chain
artifacts.description: The TEE remote-attestation chain of trust, stepped through: silicon root, CPU TDX quote, H100 attestation, on-chain DCAP verifier, signed inferences. Flip to the TEE.fail forged-quote path and watch the verifier still return valid — the crypto checks out, the premise is false.

artifacts.title: The Rebalancer's Break-Even
artifacts.description: The move-or-hold call a stablecoin yield agent makes all day, on the live Aave V3 USDC curve from Base: supply capital into a higher-quoted pool and watch your own deposit slide the realized APY down the kinked curve, then race the spread against gas. Shallow pools and L1 gas flip MOVE to HOLD.

artifacts.title: The Spoofer's Discount
artifacts.description: Drive the Proof-of-Learning trap: a logged training trajectory, audited top-Q by re-execution against a tolerance δ. Forge the run and it still passes — the forger tuned every interval under δ for 3% of training cost. Tighten δ to catch it and the honest node fails first.

artifacts.title: The Cognitive Penalty
artifacts.description: One frozen Qwen-3.5-9B judging adversarial Optimism DAO proposals, deliberation off vs on. System 1 holds every metric at 100%; reasoning drops robustness to 68.5%, flips 27% of verdicts, and costs 17x latency — a 226s window that is itself Governance-Extractable Value. Tap a row.

artifacts.title: The Shapley Split
artifacts.description: Split one DataDAO reward pool across five overlapping contributors three ways: equal split, leave-one-out, and exact Shapley value over all 2ⁿ coalitions. Drag quality sliders, drop the unique contributor, or flip on the Sybil attack and watch equal split overpay a cloned wallet.

artifacts.title: The All-Reduce Atlas
artifacts.description: Where decentralized training nodes sit on Earth and what it costs to sync them. Toggle INTELLECT-1's three measured configurations and watch the ring all-reduce span the globe: 103s inside the USA, 382s across the Atlantic, 469s once Asia joins.

artifacts.title: The Operating-Layer Lift
artifacts.description: Where reliability comes from in on-chain LLM trading agents, over DX Terminal Pro's production run: model upgrades move swap success 87% to 96%, but the operating layer takes the same weights to 99.9%. Switch panels for the prompt fixes that erased three failure modes. Tap or arrow the bars.

artifacts.title: The Byte-Equality Gate
artifacts.description: Why re-executing an LLM doesn't reproduce it. One matmul reduces to the logit gap between 'Queens, New York' and 'New York City'; drag the production split-K and watch IEEE-754 rounding flip the token at split 5 and 6, breaking the verifier's digest check. Batch-invariant kernels turn it green.

artifacts.title: The Memory-Injection Gap
artifacts.description: Why memory injection beats prompt injection against on-chain AI agents, in three switchable charts over CrAIBench: 685 attacks skewed to trading, a 55.1%-vs-0% gap on the strongest model, and the fine-tuning defense that drops attack success 85.1% to 1.7%. Tap or arrow the bars for numbers.

artifacts.title: Swarm Consensus
artifacts.description: One hard question, a swarm of LLM nodes, two ways to agree. Run a round: majority voting picks the most common answer while peer-ranked Bradley-Terry consensus surfaces the best one, and the scoreboard converges on the gap Fortytwo measured. The evaluation-edge slider shows why.

artifacts.title: The Gas Wall
artifacts.description: Forward-pass gas for five neural nets run inside the EVM, on a log axis against the live Ethereum (60M) and Base (400M) block-gas ceilings. Toggle ML2SC's measured ~106k gas/edge vs an optimized ~1.5k floor, slide the gas price for a USD readout, and watch an MNIST net blow past 180 Ethereum blocks.

artifacts.title: Web-Proof Trust
artifacts.description: The zkTLS trust boundary, explorable: switch between Plain TLS, MPC-TLS, Proxy-TLS and TEE-TLS to see where the session key lives and whom you must trust, then hit "forge the value" — plain TLS accepts the lie, the other three catch it at different costs.

artifacts.title: The Corruption Ledger
artifacts.description: Push the cost-of-corruption inequality for a restaking-secured AI oracle: set bonded stake, slash rate, audit probability, and value-at-stake, then add AVSs to watch the overloading attack flip the verdict from secure to exploitable.

artifacts.title: The Bet Machine
artifacts.description: A real Omen prediction market on Gnosis, replayed bet by bet: eight AI-agent trades walked P(YES) from 50% to 42% in 13 hours. Tap any bet to rewind the pools, then step in as the ninth bettor — set your estimate, bankroll, and stake, and compare it to the Kelly bet an agent would place.

artifacts.title: Royalty Stack
artifacts.description: Story Protocol's two royalty policies, runnable: tap any IP asset in a derivative chain to pay 100 WIP into it and watch LAP give every ancestor its absolute cut until the stack hits 100% and mints revert, while LRP compounds hop by hop and dilutes the original to dust.

artifacts.title: Blast Radius
artifacts.description: What a hijacked agent key costs under three custody models: a raw EOA key loses the whole wallet instantly, an expiry-only session key does too, and a per-period spend permission caps the bleed. Drag the sliders — or load a real 35.97 USDC/day permission pulled off Base — and watch the staircase.

artifacts.title: Nullifier Gate
artifacts.description: Semaphore's double-signal defense, explorable: send transactions to spend month-scoped nullifiers PBH-style, replay a spent proof to watch the gate revert with the real contract errors, and roll the month to see the external nullifier change reset the quota.

artifacts.title: The Protocol Gap
artifacts.description: Seven years of the Elliptic AML benchmark in four switchable charts: the 2019 table everyone forgot, the 2026 leakage-free re-ranking, one GraphSAGE trained on four different graphs, and the F1 cliff at time step 43. Hover, tap, or tab across the bars for exact precision and recall.

artifacts.title: BME Equilibrium
artifacts.description: Render's Burn-Mint Equilibrium with the real protocol constants: drag the demand and price sliders to see monthly burns race the 492,132 RENDER emission schedule, toggle RNP-023's Salad flows on, and find the demand level where the network actually stops inflating.

artifacts.title: The Bandwidth Wall
artifacts.description: How much data one GPU ships per optimizer step: AdamW-DDP vs DeMo's DCT+top-k compression, on a log scale. Toggle OLMo-300M ↔ OLMo-1B, hover a bar for exact MB/step and reduction factor, and slide the link speed to turn megabytes into seconds-per-step. Data: DeMo paper, Table 1 (arXiv:2411.19870).

artifacts.title: The Price of Trust
artifacts.description: Every route to trustworthy AI inference, priced on one log axis: TEE attestation at 1.07×, optimistic re-execution at 2–4×, zkML and FHE at 10³–10⁵×, verifiable FHE beyond. Hover, tap, or arrow through the bars to see what each overhead actually buys — and whom you still trust.

artifacts.title: Emission Engine
artifacts.description: Run the same emission-capture attack against both of Bittensor's allocation regimes: a refundable constant-product price pump (dTAO, pre-Nov 2025) versus an EMA-smoothed staking flow with a 30-day half-life (TaoFlow). Real protocol constants show why one pays instantly and the other decays.

artifacts.title: Attention Lens
artifacts.description: Transformer attention made visible: hover or tap any token in the sentence and watch weighted arcs reach for the tokens it attends to, with glow proportional to attention weight. Left alone, the lens auto-cycles through the sequence.

artifacts.title: Merkle Cascade
artifacts.description: An interactive Merkle tree: click any leaf to watch its hash cascade hop by hop to the root, with the sibling hashes that form the inclusion proof highlighted along the way — four hashes prove one of sixteen leaves.

artifacts.title: Gradient Descent
artifacts.description: A glowing marker performs literal gradient descent over a 3D loss landscape — analytic gradients, momentum, and a fading trail. Drag to orbit the terrain; click anywhere on it to drop a new starting point.

artifacts.title: Synapse Chain
artifacts.description: The blokz brand visual, explorable: a shimmering neural cluster bridged by a particle stream to a minting block lattice. Drag to orbit the bridge; click to fire a thought across it and mint a block on arrival.

artifacts.title: Falsifier Gate
artifacts.description: An agentic audit swarm's load-bearing stage: hypothesis particles leave the contract and hold at the falsifier gate while a proof-of-concept runs — hallucinated findings burst into debris, executable ones pass into the report. Tap a code line to plant a bug and watch the swarm catch it.

artifacts.title: Dispute Bisection
artifacts.description: A fraud-proof dispute game you can rig: tap any step of the computation trace to plant a fault, then watch the chain bisect proposer vs watcher commitments — six queries isolate the one divergent step, it gets re-executed on-chain, and the liar's bond is slashed.

artifacts.title: Neural Flow
artifacts.description: Forward passes through a small feed-forward network, animated: signals ripple layer to layer, weights set the glow, and activations heat the neurons they reach.

artifacts.title: Block Mesh
artifacts.description: A live 3D peer-to-peer network: nodes on a fuzzy sphere, gossip links between nearest peers, and transaction pulses propagating hop by hop across the topology.
